title: Demagnetize a solid robot-joint shaft through a low-frequency tunnel
objective: Grasp a representative solid ferromagnetic robot-joint shaft, align it with a round low-frequency demagnetizing tunnel, physically carry its full length through the alternating-field region, and place it in a clean output cradle with reduced simulated remanence, without collision, dropping, reversal-induced remagnetization, or particle recontamination.
skills: stable grasping of an elongated rigid shaft
orientation control under pose-dependent magnetic forces
success_conditions: Full success requires every shaft material cell to traverse the effective field, a validated hysteresis calculation to finish below the frozen representative remanence threshold, stable placement in the clean cradle, and no tunnel contact, drop, unsafe release, contamination-zone contact, or excessive device thermal load. Alignment and incomplete treatment earn partial credit. Waypoint traversal alone, direct magnetic-state writes, pose or velocity injection, collision suppression, or a hidden success flag cannot score. A physically valid one-arm strategy receives full credit.
industrial_value: The manufacturer identifies shafts as suitable products for low-frequency tunnel demagnetization. Separate bearing-industry guidance requires demagnetizing components that contact bearings and documents particle adhesion, denting, vibration, and wear from residual magnetism. A representative robot-joint shaft treated before bearing assembly therefore has direct robot-building relevance.
dexterity: The central manipulation is carrying a long, solid part through a confined aperture while preserving clearance and orientation as its magnetic state and field-derived forces evolve. It is materially harder than pick-and-place, yet remains a rigid-body task within pinned-YAM reach after fixture scaling; no artificial bimanual requirement is imposed.

evidence.locator: Industrial magnetic handling and demagnetization brochure, page 18, “Low-frequency demagnetizing tunnels”
Industrial magnetic handling and demagnetization brochure, page 18, “Low-frequency demagnetizing tunnels”
Modelica Magnetic FluxTubes UsersGuide, StaticHysteresis.Tellinen, “The Tellinen hysteresis model”

asset_plan: Author a representative, explicitly non-product-replica rigid tunnel, 320 mm solid shaft, input stand, clean output cradle, and guarded field enclosure. Freeze aperture, shaft diameter and mass, field-zone length, material envelope curve, remanence limit, force ceiling, thermal duty, and reach bounds before development. Use a Tellinen hysteresis state per axial shaft cell, driven only by simulated coil field evaluated from actual poses and time in the verified native PRE/POST physics callback. Couple a bounded field-gradient force and torque into PhysX; never overwrite shaft pose, velocity, or magnetic state. Before YAM integration, test major and minor loops, proper and incomplete passage, reversal, stopping, timestep/rate convergence, force and energy finiteness, thermal accumulation, reset freshness, collision response, and reachable clean placement. The representative field calibration and protocol are disclosed prototype assumptions, not manufacturer specifications.
risk: No acquired source supplies a specific tunnel model’s proprietary aperture, waveform, field calibration, or operating speed. Those values must remain frozen representative assumptions and cannot be advertised as Goudsmit performance. Static Tellinen behavior does not by itself establish dynamic eddy-current accuracy, so the selected solid shaft must use a conservative low-frequency regime and pass convergence and improper-treatment controls. Catalog neighbor pr-1810 tests controlled passage through a narrow slot; final novelty depends on the independently validated remanence outcome and magnetic force interaction, not on the passage trajectory alone. Full catalog and six-suite clearance remains a mandatory downstream gate.
